category_title: Students performing as rhythmic, collaborative poetry readers
minimal_context: Bill and Kwame are participating in a readers' workshop where they are supposed to pair up and read poetry texts to build their stamina.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for readers' workshop. Please pair up and read your poems to each other to build your reading stamina.

STUDENT: (Taking turns reading in singing voices) This is the way! Hey! We start the day! Hey!

TUTOR: Let's just read the text on the page, please.

STUDENT: (Continuing in singing voices) We get the knowledge! Hey! To go to college! Hey!

TUTOR: Keep going, but remember the rule for readers' workshop is that it should be quiet.

STUDENT: (Tapping their pencils on the desks and moving their bodies from side to side) We won't stop there! Hey! Go anywhere! Hey! (They start singing louder and invite the peers next to them to join their rhythm)

options.A: Have a timer sound every minute, prompting the students to self-record whether they read quietly during the preceding interval on a sheet of paper, providing feedback afterward.
options.B: Use desk carrels to provide areas of personal space and make a clear distinction between individual versus partner reading areas.
options.C: Gather data on appropriate quiet reading behavior and disruptive singing behavior using a scatter plot during the readers' workshop sessions.
options.D: Invite the students to participate in choral reading of a shared poetry text during the readers' workshop sessions.
